title: Steve Lewis and Walter Pichon, piano styles
summary: After a garbled exchange about Richard Jones, Mason discusses pianists Steve Lewis and Walter Pichon and their ragtime and cocktail styles.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did you ever know Richard Jones? Richard M. Jones? Richard Jones.

I know Steve, yes, Steve Lewis. Did you like his playing? Well of course he played a style that was quite popular at that time when I heard it. You see they had ragtime piano plays at that time and this music like Swinging Down the Lane and those tunes of course, they were not so popular around there we played them on the boat but of course they were not so popular around the city. I had Swinging Down the Lane and Lord's Nest and let me see here, and another tune that we used to play on the boat that, well those slow tunes of course were not so popular around at that time down there and their band, Pichon's band didn't do much at that playing. Of course, but he played nice piano. But of course the style of piano that a man needed to play now to play most of these tunes is what they call a kind of prelude style of playing, which is quite different from what they call ragtime piano playing. And that's one of the reasons I think that you didn't hear much, the fellas didn't concentrate much on that slow style of, or what they call cocktail style of piano playing.
Oh yeah, I don't mean Walter, Walter is a different piano player altogether from Steve, Steve Lewis I was speaking of.
I mean you mentioned the Pichon. Oh yeah, Pichon, oh yes.

That was Walter. Walter, yes. Walter Pichon, he's one of the piano player. He's still going. Yeah, he came here, you know, he played here in St. Louis, he was up to town and country. He played down there's another very fine club in St. Louis over here on Washington Avenue. He came in and played for quite a long time. I forgot the name of that place. Anyway, he was a very fine piano player and I liked his style. He played, kind of played the style of Fats Waller. They even called him Fats. Yeah, that's right. Yeah, they did, they called him Fats.
